subject: Discovery recap: token-cost constraints & pilot proposal
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Jules Martin <jules@soylabs.com>
Cc: karthik@redwood.com, monica@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-14T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery recap: token-cost constraints & pilot proposal

Hi Jules — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

What you told us (pain points):
- Token spend is the single biggest line item for your conversational assistant; engineering says ~60% of requests are short queries but a long-tail 10% of sessions (long context) drive the majority of tokens.
- Current infra is overprovisioned for bursty payroll windows; you're seeing big variance month-over-month.
- Batching is being limited to preserve latency (p50 ~140–180ms) which means lower GPU utilization.
- Team is cautious about accuracy loss from quantization, but open to experiments if we can measure end-user impact.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Reduce per-token cost by ~40%–50% for the 80% of production traffic without degrading p50 latency beyond 200ms for interactive flows.
- Maintain or improve answer quality on existing NLU tests (internal label set).
- Pilot throughput target: sustain the typical peak traffic pattern (bursts up to 3x baseline) for 2 weeks without SLA-weighted errors.

How Redwood proposes to approach this pilot:
1) Run a 2-week connected pilot using a dedicated sandbox model variant + continuous batching and prefix KV caching for dialog.
2) Start with conservative quantization (per-channel INT8 on a copy of the model) and run automated quality regression on your eval set before serving traffic.
3) Track token-level cost, model latency (p50/p95), and quality regressions on each rollout.

Immediate asks from your side:
- Share a representative sample of 2k–5k request/response pairs (anonymized) and current billing export (we can accept CSV).
- Confirm whether we have permission to run INT8 experiments on a sandboxed copy of the model.
- Tech sync (30–45m) with your infra lead + our inference engineer (Karthik) — propose Tue 2027-02-22 or Wed 2027-02-23.

Attachments: example-workload-sample.jsonl (sample payloads), current-pricing-export.csv (billing export stub).

Next steps (what I'll do):
- Karthik will draft a pilot plan and a short SOW template for scope & deliverables.
- I'll open the HubSpot opportunity (SOY-4021) and share a Drive folder for artifacts.

If that matches your memory, reply with: (a) confirm sample + billing share, (b) preferred tech-sync slot, (c) any legal/security blockers (SOC2 / data retention).

Thanks — Hannah

Thanks Hannah — that recap is accurate and helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 40%–50% target is ambitious but reasonable if we can get strong batching gains and a caching layer. Would be ok to aim for a 40% baseline improvement in pilot and then iterate.
- Latency tolerance: for interactive consumer flows let's cap p50 at 200ms; for internal batch scoring (nightly) we can tolerate higher latency.
- Quantization: engineering is willing to try INT8 in a sandbox, but we need a clear rollback plan and pre/post quality metrics.

Security ask: can you share Redwood's SOC2 status and your data retention / deletion policy for pilot data? I’ve cc'd our platform team alias so Monica can follow up on technical details.

We will upload a 2k anonymized sample and the billing export to the Drive link you mentioned by EOD tomorrow.

Tech-sync: Tue 2027-02-22 works for us at 11:00 PT.

— Jules

Quick technical note from the inference side — thanks for the context. Short plan and blockers I want to flag: 

1) Batching strategy: we can run continuous batching with adaptive time windowing to preserve p50 latency. For interactive traffic we expect 20%–35% batching uplift; for burst windows this can be higher. We will tune the batching window per route.

2) Caching: prefix KV caching for dialog will reduce repeated prefix tokens. To be effective we need 24–48h of representative session logs to compute hit-rate estimates.

3) Quantization: recommend "shadow" experiments where INT8 runs in parallel on a shadow replica (no user traffic) and we compute automated quality diffs on your labeled set. If diffs are within tolerance we'll promote to canary. This requires: (a) your labeled eval set (200–500 items), (b) a small batch of golden responses for regression checks.

4) Metrics we will track per release: token-cost per request, p50/p95 latency, infer error-rate (429/5xx), and evaluation AUC on the labeled set.

If you can share the anonymized sample + billing export, I’ll run an initial cost model and share a baseline report before the tech sync. Happy to host the technical sync and walk through what I’d tune first.

— Karthik
